Dispatch scoped repair to sapience/nix/lean permissions.allow. Measurement found a fourth stale record not named in the dispatch: email's permissions.deny (7 items, tracked items: []), same dedup-before-track defect. Also found the defect class covers non-matcher hook-event arrays (sapience's SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit/SessionEnd/Stop), not only permission arrays, contradicting the dispatch's blanket 'hooks escape this' framing for those four events specifically.

Plan phase re-validated the research report's scope-item-2 recommendation ([Regenerate]/manager.wipe repairs the stale tracking records) and found it incorrect: manager.regenerate calls settings_backup.restore BEFORE manager.resync_all, and settings_backup.BACKUP_FILES includes settings.local.json, so the wipe path restores the already-populated grant list as the merge base and the dedup-before-track defect fires again. The plan therefore selects a different repair route (plain redeploy AFTER the engine fix) and a different tracking shape than the report recommended.

merge_spec.lua is already 3-failed/21-passed headless before any change: read_host_fixture points at specs/369_orphan_sweep_for_removed_merge_target_entries/records/fixtures/host-settings.json, a task directory that no longer exists after archival/renumbering. The plan adds a first phase to recover the fixture from commit fc8cca3f0 and re-site it next to the spec, since the task's acceptance bar requires merge_spec to pass headless.

Phase 2's verification step asserts the merge_spec.lua baseline stays 24/0/0 after the deep_merge tracking fix, and the research report's mcpServers verdict (adopted in the plan's Overview/Research Integration) claims mcpServers is structurally immune to the dedup-before-track defect because a first-time key insertion is tracked as new_object regardless of nested fields. Both are only partially true: mcpServers.<name> key insertion IS immune, but a NESTED array field inside an already-merged mcp server config object (e.g. mcpServers.fixture.args) reaches the SAME plain-array arm as permissions.allow on a second merge, and therefore inherits the exact same complete-tracking fix -- flipping merge_spec.lua's pre-existing 'requirement (c)' test from green to red, since that test asserted the second merge's tracked result is a true no-op (the old dedup-before-track behavior). Corrected the test in Phase 2 (rather than deferring to Phase 4) with a comment explaining why, since Phase 2's own verification gate requires a clean spec run before Phase 3 begins. Flagging for Phase 5's mcpServers re-confirmation task: the verdict needs qualifying -- top-level key insertion is immune; nested array fields within an already-existing key are not.

class: scope boundary discovered during test authoring
what_happened: While writing Phase 4's sibling-extension-retention spec case, discovered that M.unmerge_settings's opts.retained_fragments guard (Phase 2) only protects per-item removal in the 'appended' and 'hook_merged' items branches, exactly as the plan's Phase 2 task list specifies. It does NOT protect the wholesale-removal types ('new_array', 'new_object', 'new_value'), which unconditionally set t[key] = nil regardless of opts. Concretely: if the FIRST-ever extension to populate a shared array (e.g. permissions.allow) is unloaded while a sibling extension's own later contribution still sits in that same on-disk array, the wholesale removal discards the sibling's item too, because the unloading extension's OWN tracked record for that key was fixed at 'new_array' when it was loaded (first), and never changes. This is pre-existing behavior unchanged by this task's fix (the wholesale-removal unconditional deletion predates Phase 2), and does not affect the four stale records this task repairs (sapience/nix/lean's permissions.allow and email's permissions.deny are all already non-empty in this repository before these extensions ever merge in, so their own tracked type is 'appended', never 'new_array'). Recording as a known scope boundary for Phase 5's documentation rather than extending Phase 2/3's guard to the wholesale-removal types, which would be a larger, riskier change (new_object wholesale removal also backs mcpServers.<name> and other non-array merge targets) not requested by the plan.

Phase 5's verification criterion ('bash .claude/scripts/verify-deploy.sh --skip-slow --only-gate 3,4 /home/benjamin/.config/nvim exits 0') currently fails on gate 3 (doc-lint), but exclusively because of a PRE-EXISTING sapience extension staleness unrelated to this task: deployed script content drift on scripts/install-sapience-mcp-session-hook.sh, and two stale index-entries.json line_count declarations for sapience's per-repo-scoping.md and injection-site-scoping.md. This matches the dispatch's own deploy-freshness-context block, present before any phase of this task started. Confirmed via bash .claude/scripts/check-extension-docs.sh that the nvim extension itself (this phase's own edit target) reports clean ('[nvim] OK', no finding at all, not even a line_count drift). Gate 4 (task-reference lint) passes standalone. Phase 6's own redeploy (bash .claude/scripts/deploy-headless.sh) is expected to resolve the sapience staleness as a side effect, and Phase 6 re-runs the full bash .claude/scripts/verify-deploy.sh as its own verification, so this is deferred to that step rather than fixed here (fixing sapience's deploy drift is out of this task's edit scope).
